facts.claim: The frozen 4B claim build on the bounty-style set (V-para) delivers about a quarter of the frontier reference's value above "nothing", and loses every head-to-head.
facts.value: raw 0.413 (0.384–0.445); floor-adjusted 0.261 (0.224–0.300); win/tie/loss 0/0/51 in both seeds
facts.set_status: held-out for this run (cut 3 on 2026-10-05, cut 6 on 2026-10-06); dev-style for everything measured after 2026-10-06
facts.caveat: Cut 7 = cut 6 on this set (the FACTS table fires 0 times on it). Public BAR-TABLE prints CI high 0.300; one claim draft prints 0.299 (rounding).

facts.claim: The same 4B claim build on the second set (v0.2, later burnt to dev).
facts.set_status: held-out at run time; burnt → dev by ruling 2026-10-06
facts.caveat: Claim draft v4.2.4 (§0 and Appendix A) carries the cut-3 values 0.513 / 0.389; the cut-6 = cut-7 values here are the ones to publish.

facts.claim: A system that declines every question already scores about 0.31 on the raw ratio, because the rubric never goes below 1 of 5.
facts.caveat: This is why the floor-adjusted ratio, not the raw ratio, is the headline.

facts.claim: Bar status: no configuration reaches 0.50 on the primary (floor-adjusted) reading; the formal raw rule is met only on development data by the deep tier with thinking.
facts.value: best floor-adjusted on V-para = 0.436 (CI high 0.472), short by 0.064; formal raw rule (CI low > 0.50) met by deep + thinking on dev data only (desktop; the v0.2 leg of the 512 budget is 1 seed); 0 wins on every Claude-judged row of V-para and v0.2
facts.caveat: Never present as "bar reached". Under the Claude judge on held-out data the bar was not reached.

facts.claim: Swapping in the 35B mixture-of-experts deep tier (no thinking) raises the bounty-style score.
facts.caveat: Desktop only; the deep tier has never run on a phone.

facts.claim: Deep tier (no thinking) on v0.2.
Letting the deep tier think for up to 1024 tokens before answering.
Thinking is the largest single measured gain on the bounty-style set.
facts.value: thinking (1024) vs no thinking: raw +0.075 (+0.040…+0.110); floor-adjusted +0.093 (+0.050…+0.137)

facts.claim: Recommended deep configuration (35B mixture-of-experts + 512-token thinking budget) on the bounty-style set.
facts.value: raw 0.553 (0.524–0.581; with seed noise 0.513–0.592); floor-adjusted 0.436 (0.401–0.472; with seed noise 0.387–0.486); win 0/51; desktop p50 ≈ 79 s
facts.ci: 95 % item bootstrap; common-mode CI adds seed noise
facts.caveat: Chosen as the best of ≥ 8 deep configurations on this same set: expect a winner's-curse discount of about 0.01–0.02. QUEUE prints raw 0.552; the two-seed aggregate is 0.553. Desktop only.

facts.claim: A 512-token thinking budget matches 1024 in quality at about half the time.
facts.caveat: Verdict label: CHEAPER-PARITY (an equivalence, not a gain).

facts.claim: A 256-work budget is cheaper but measurably worse.
facts.caveat: Keeps ≈ 63 % of the thinking gain at 40 % of the time.

facts.claim: Three seeds of the recommended deep configuration show how much one run can move.
Recommended deep configuration on v0.2: the first point above 0.50 floor-adjusted on any set, with a CI that straddles 0.50.
facts.caveat: One seed, development data, desktop only.

facts.claim: Deep tier with 1024-token thinking on v0.2.
Anchor: a small frontier model with no web access (Claude Haiku 5.5) on the bounty-style set.
facts.ci: raw 95 % item bootstrap; floor-adjusted CI never computed
facts.caveat: The best deep configuration (0.436, CI high 0.472) does not reach this anchor either.

facts.claim: Win-rate against the frontier reference: zero on both bounty-relevant sets under the Claude judge; a few isolated wins exist only on the public dev set.
facts.value: 0 wins on every row and seed of V-para and v0.2 (Opus); v0.1 dev: 1/57 under Opus for the deep R450, LES and 4B rows; 2/57 under Haiku on the 12 GB-class phone run
facts.judge: Claude Opus; Claude Haiku L1 (phone run)
facts.caveat: Public text that says "0 everywhere" (boar-research README.md:42, boar-bench TRACE-FORMAT.md:70) overstates the scope.

facts.claim: A judge from a different model family scores everything higher on V-para, but keeps the ranking and the near-zero win-rate.
facts.value: 4B: raw 0.497 (0.449–0.547), floor-adjusted 0.361; deep + think 512: raw 0.667 (0.621–0.711), floor-adjusted 0.577 (0.519–0.632); deep − 4B +0.171 (+0.123…+0.219) vs +0.139 under Claude; per-item Spearman 0.88–0.92; win-rate 0.00–0.01
facts.ci: 95 % item bootstrap (4B floor-adjusted CI not in the sources read)
facts.judge: cross-family: OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol (via the Codex CLI) (post-hoc, not pre-registered)
facts.caveat: Post-hoc and not pre-registered; it is the only point above 0.50 floor-adjusted on V-para and exists only under the cross-family judge; the lower-judge rule keeps the Claude number as headline.

facts.claim: The cross-family judge on v0.2.
facts.value: 4B: raw 0.617 (0.567–0.666), floor-adjusted 0.517 (2 seeds); deep + think 512: raw 0.714 (0.666–0.759), floor-adjusted 0.639 (0.579–0.695) (1 seed); deep − 4B +0.097 vs +0.096 under Claude; Spearman 0.90–0.97; win-rate 2.7 % / 6.4 % vs 0 % under Claude
facts.judge: cross-family: OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol (via the Codex CLI) (post-hoc, not pre-registered)
facts.caveat: Post-hoc. The Claude judge is the stricter family by ≈ 0.10 on both sets; the offset is stable across sets and arms.

facts.claim: Re-judging the exact same answers barely moves the score: judge noise is negligible next to seed noise.
facts.value: σ_judge ≈ 0.003 raw / 0.004 floor-adjusted; per-item r 0.96; same winner 51/51

facts.claim: Seed noise: the same deep configuration run with two random seeds differs by more than many tested "levers".
facts.value: s42 vs s43, same configuration: Δ −0.039 (−0.072…−0.011) raw; house rule since 2026-10-16: a one-seed deep-tier Δ below 0.05 on V-para is seed noise (raised from 0.03)
facts.caveat: The public boar-research README.md:77 still says 0.03.

facts.claim: Part of the gap to the reference is length: shortening the references to 80 words raises the deep tier's score, mostly through completeness and usefulness.
facts.value: deep + think 512 floor-adjusted 0.412 → 0.514 (0.456–0.578) with ≤ 80-word references; paired +0.102 (+0.068…+0.144); ≈ 17 % of the gap is length, 83 % substance
facts.caveat: Diagnostic with altered references; not a bar reading.

facts.claim: On correctness alone the deep tier is much closer to the reference than on the full rubric.
facts.caveat: Single-axis diagnostic, not a bar reading.

facts.claim: On a real 12 GB-class phone, in airplane mode, the frozen build gives the same judged quality as on the desktop.
facts.value: phone raw 0.529 (0.481–0.575) vs desktop 0.529; floor-adjusted 0.403 vs 0.402; paired −0.000 (−0.026…+0.028); 72/72 answered; fast-tier p50 30.7 s; app memory (PSS) peak 5.88 GB during model load, then ≤ 4.23 GB
facts.judge: Claude Haiku 5.5-low (L1 triage judge, N = 4, both orders)
facts.caveat: Haiku-judged level; not comparable with Opus-judged ratios. The device has 10.7 GiB usable RAM.

facts.claim: Earlier, on an 8 GB phone, cut 6 also matched the desktop.
facts.value: phone 0.561 (0.507–0.617) vs desktop 0.558 / 0.560; 73/73 answered; PSS max 4.41 GiB
facts.caveat: Opus-judged; not comparable in level with the Haiku-judged 12 GB-class run.

facts.claim: One matching knowledge pack helps the small model a little on questions written from that pack.
facts.caveat: Pack-matched dev questions, not a bounty-bar measurement.

facts.claim: Installing all packs at once crowds out the right passage and costs a little quality.
Ceiling test: handing the model the exact fact-bearing chunk shows the headroom is retrieval, not reading.
facts.value: inject fact chunk (ADD) +0.095 (+0.070…+0.122); fact chunk only (ONLY) +0.115 (+0.088…+0.142)
facts.caveat: Oracle (cheating) cell: an upper bound, not a deployable result.

facts.claim: The one retrieval change that converted: append the retrieved article's neighbouring chunks plus a few vector-search candidates, under a 600-work budget (HEADPASS-X2b).
facts.value: Opus +0.066 (+0.043…+0.091); Haiku +0.056; fact chunk present in context 35 → 102 of 180
facts.caveat: LEVER on pack-matched dev data only; inert on the claim kit (ceiling ≈ 0.011) and not a bounty-bar lever.

facts.claim: The 35B deep tier gains nothing measurable from packs; its advantage over the 4B with the same pack is model knowledge.
facts.value: deep with vs without pack Δ −0.002 (−0.020…+0.016); deep − 4B with the same pack +0.054 (+0.034…+0.073)
facts.judge: Claude Haiku 5.5-low (L1 triage judge, N = 4, both orders)

facts.claim: Long conversations do not degrade answers up to turn 15.
facts.value: turns 6–15, in-session vs standalone: 1.136 (0.993–1.320); self-contained items 1.017 (0.950–1.095); latency ≈ 22 s vs 8 s at turns 14–15
facts.judge: Claude Haiku 5.5-low (L1 triage judge, N = 4, both orders)
facts.caveat: The reference here is BOAR's own standalone answer, not the frontier reference: a ratio of ratios, not a bar number.

facts.claim: Four days of an unattended agent research loop produced one dev-only lever.
facts.value: 133 ticks (28 idle), 2026-10-11 12:10 → 10-14 19:09; ≈ 10.5k judge calls (Opus 4,851 + Haiku 5,660) plus 1,491 Haiku writer/generation calls; Mac mini 44.4 h + MacBook 18.1 h of generation; ≈ 31 h avoidable

facts.claim: Early ceiling test on the public dev set: even the gold passage leaves the 4B below a no-web frontier model.
facts.value: raw: closed-book 0.487; full engine 0.507; with the gold passage 0.606; Claude Haiku without web 0.653
facts.caveat: Raw ratios only; floor-adjusted values were not computed.

facts.claim: The first deep-tier test was the first lever to beat noise.
facts.caveat: Raw ratio on the public dev set.

facts.claim: Mixture-of-experts models in the 25–35B class form one closed-book plateau, well above the 4B.
facts.value: closed-book raw: Gemma 4 26B-A4B 0.613; Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 0.603; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 0.596; vs 4B 0.487
facts.caveat: Screen differences between the MoE models are not detected at MDE 0.055.

facts.claim: Projected phone time for the recommended deep configuration (never measured on a phone).
facts.value: ≈ 1.9–2.8 min per answer at thinking budget 512 on a 12 GB phone CPU (third-party public decode rates of 4–6 tok/s + BOAR arithmetic); the 2026-10-09 estimate of 3.5–5 min was for budget 1024
facts.caveat: Third-party rates, not a BOAR measurement.

facts.claim: An expert-streaming engine runs the 35B model in under 3 GiB of RAM on a desktop CPU with judged-equivalent answers.
facts.value: judged 0.625 vs llama-server 0.634, paired −0.010 (−0.042…+0.018); RSS 2.75–2.81 GiB; 14–17 tok/s on the Mac mini CPU; 10/10 greedy-identical vs the fork base

facts.claim: The on-device MoE engine (bmoe) is not token-identical to the desktop server but is judged equivalent on identical contexts.
facts.caveat: An equivalence, not a lever: lets desktop deep-tier numbers transfer to a bmoe device plan with this caveat.
